String Methods

The one idea to landA string method never changes your string. It hands you back a new one, and the only thing you have to get right is where it stops. [start:end:step] stops before end; strip works in from each end and stops at the first character that is not in the set, so anything in the middle is never even looked at.

Worksheet task 3 Fill the table yourself first. Nothing here moves until hands are off keyboards.
Line 1 pin holds eight characters. The grey dots are the two spaces at each end.
Line 2 strip with nothing in the brackets takes spaces off each end. On the left it stops at 0, on the right it stops at 2.
Line 3 strip("0") takes the 0 off the left. On the right it meets 2, which is not a 0, so it stops there and looks no further.
Line 4 Everything left is a digit, so isdigit gives True and line 5 runs.
Line 5 The slice starts at 0 and jumps two, so it lands on the first and the third of what is left.
Lines 6 and 7 Neither of them ever ran. The else belongs to a question that was already answered yes, so it is skipped and it stays skipped.

Exit: one question

Exit question
Which one prints nothing?
An app asks for a 4 digit PIN. For which one of these does the screen show nothing at all?
1pin = input()
2pin = pin.strip("-0")
3if pin.isdigit():
4    if len(pin) == 4:
5        print("Valid")
  • The user types 0-4748-0
  • The user types -4-748-
  • The user types 00474800
  • The user types -47480-
Option B. Both ends come off down to '4-748'. The dash in the middle was never reached, so isdigit is False and line 4 is never even asked. Nothing is printed.
